title: The Vow of Bellbird Bay
premise: Mara Ashgrove fled Bellbird Bay after a career-ending stage collapse left her hand scarred and her confidence shattered, hiding out in her late grandmother's failing bakery with a lease that expires in spring. When a snowstorm traps her with Theo Vance—the rival cellist who witnessed her collapse—and Jonah Reyes, the first love she abandoned a decade ago, the forced proximity cracks open every truth she's buried: the collapse wasn't her fault, and neither was leaving. As the storm isolates the town and the three of them reckon with old betrayals, Mara must choose between a safe silence and the terrifying vulnerability of playing again. She ends the book performing one small, imperfect piece at the bakery's reopening—forgiving herself, choosing Jonah, and signing a new lease on her own terms.
about_author: Bram Eriksen is the pen name of a former orchestra librarian turned small-town bookseller who writes romances about second chances and the music people make after the applause stops. They live on a windswept peninsula with a rescue greyhound and an unreasonable number of sheet music anthologies.

chapters.title: The Quiet Between Movements
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Six months after her collapse, Mara runs her grandmother's bakery in Bellbird Bay, her cello gathering dust in the back room. A lease notice arrives with thirty days' warning. Emotional beat: numb routine shattered by a deadline she can't outrun.

chapters.title: Snowfall and Strangers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A freak blizzard closes the coastal road, stranding Theo Vance—the rival cellist whose recording session brought him through town—and Jonah Reyes, back to settle his late aunt's estate. Emotional beat: dread curdling into trapped intimacy as the power flickers out.

chapters.title: What the Storm Brought In
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah recognizes Mara instantly and says nothing, helping her board up windows by candlelight. Theo watches them with a cellist's ear for unplayed tension. Emotional beat: old love resurfacing as warmth Mara refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Night Theo Talked
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo reveals he was in the audience the night of Mara's collapse—and that he saw the rigging crew's error, the one her management buried to protect the venue. Emotional beat: the first crack in Mara's guilt, delivered by the last person she'd trust.

chapters.title: Flour, Salt, and Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Baking bread by generator light, Mara and Jonah finally argue about why she left him a decade ago—her fear that loving him meant staying small in a town that would never let her play. Emotional beat: grief and anger entwined, neither able to apologize first.

chapters.title: Letters in the Attic
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah finds his aunt's letters revealing she'd been quietly paying Mara's lease as a gift, hoping she'd stay. He realizes Mara's 'failure' was a wound the whole town helped bandage wrong. Emotional beat: tenderness complicated by the discovery that everyone conspired in her hiding.

chapters.title: The Rigging Report
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Theo produces the venue's suppressed safety inspection he's carried for two years, unable to use it without her consent. Mara must decide whether to go public and reclaim her name, or stay invisible and lose the bakery anyway. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The roads open; Theo leaves for his recording, and Jonah's estate sale looms, meaning his departure too. Alone in the bakery, Mara takes the cello from its case for the first time and plays four broken bars, weeping. Emotional beat: the turn—forgiveness of the person in the mirror begins.

chapters.title: One Small, Imperfect Piece
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with Jonah's interlude. At the bakery's community-organized reopening, Mara signs the new lease, then plays a short piece on a borrowed cello—flawed, trembling, alive. Jonah stays. Emotional beat: the climax as vulnerability, not spectacle.

chapters.title: Bellbird Song
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Weeks later, spring arrives: Theo sends a recording of his album dedicated to 'the cellist who taught me courage,' and Mara teaches a Saturday music class in the bakery's back room with Jonah beside her. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not stumbled into—the vow finally kept.
